_comment: Controlled vocabulary for the ServerOS Space Resolver.
This file is DATA. It declares three orthogonal dimensions and a deliberately
small placement policy. It carries no observed state, no counts, no hashes,
and no cloud paths: a concrete locator is an ADAPTER concern, never a
resolver concern. See space/schema.yaml for the reasoning.

surface._comment: WHERE an object physically lives. Stable across reorganisations.

values.local: local filesystem under WORKSPACE_ROOT or DATA_ROOT
values.git: a local Git working tree or worktree
values.wiki: a curated Feishu Wiki space tree
values.minutes: a Feishu Minutes object (no folder hierarchy exists)
values.mydocs: My Document Library: a Feishu Wiki-provider space (space_type=my_library) with node/subpage hierarchy, not a Drive-style folder tree

object_type._comment: WHAT the object physically is. Never a placement policy.

_comment: WHY the object exists. Surface-neutral by construction: a physical surface
name must never appear in a role. `drive-project`, `drive-meeting`,
`drive-staging` and `minute-sidecar` were retired for exactly that reason.
`unclassified` is a real value: it means a human or Agent must decide, and
the resolver must not guess on its behalf.

values.workbench: an operating surface a human works in day to day
values.knowledge: durable architecture / method knowledge worth keeping
values.meeting: the logical entity of one meeting across surfaces
values.method: a reusable method, convention or procedure
values.source: an authoritative source object, including raw or external
values.deliverable: a formal acceptance or handover artifact
values.inbox: loose personal authoring not yet classified
values.residue: leftover output awaiting a human cleanup decision
values.unclassified: no role has been decided yet

surface_object_types._comment: A (surface, object_type) pair outside this table is structurally invalid.

_comment: One rule per (surface, semantic_role). Absence of a rule is NOT a default to
the observed surface: it yields PROPOSAL_REQUIRED, because a rule that does
not exist cannot justify a move. Rules carry a LOGICAL target only.
`strength: canonical` means the rule follows from the surface contract;
`strength: default` means it is a convention that a human may override.
The `mydocs` block splits one curation duty into two, which is why it reads
the way it does. My Document Library is the WORKBENCH: workbench, project,
work-item, report and deliverable material is canonical there and does not
move. Only knowledge and method are promoted, because those outlive the work
that produced them. An earlier version promoted all seven to the knowledge
surface, which was correct only while a single curated tree held both roles.
`mydocs`/`meeting` is deliberately ABSENT. A meeting's canon is the Minute
(`minutes`/`meeting` and `minutes`/`source` below), and its sidecars are Drive
files; no curated meeting index exists on a Wiki surface, so a meeting-role
object authored on the workbench is a question for a human, not a lookup.
Absence here is the rule set working, not a rule set with a hole.

rules.note: My Document Library is the loose authoring / inbox surface. Staying is correct.
A short-lived note may stay personal; a human may still promote it.
Aged-unclassified objects are proposed for classification, never auto-moved.
My Document Library IS the workbench surface; its root node is the Current View.
Project working material belongs on the workbench, not on the knowledge surface.
An Item's durable material is authored on the workbench; the Item id names it, it is not a folder layer.
A human-readable report is workbench material and is canonical where it was authored.
Durable knowledge outlives the work that produced it and is canonical on a knowledge surface.
A reusable method is knowledge, not workbench material.
A source may belong in Wiki or Drive; the resolver refuses to choose alone.
Evidence normally belongs to a Run under DATA_ROOT, not to Feishu.
Minutes keeps the native object and gets a logical index; it is never a Drive file.
Deleting or adopting residue is a human decision. Propose, do not move.
Local cleanup is a human decision and is never auto-applied.

_comment: A logical index is a locator-only entry, never a second copy of a body.
`index` is reported when the object is already canonical but unindexed.
index_kinds.deliverable-index: a project's delivery index entry pointing at the canonical object
index_kinds.meeting-entry: a curated meeting entry pointing at the Minute and its sidecars

_comment: The resolver never grants a write. Cross-surface moves are always proposals:
on Feishu 'add to wiki' is a MOVE with no automatic undo, so it stays behind
an explicit human gate.
